key_insight: Se/ZnMgO photodiodes act as self-powered visual synapses where the wavelength of light alone determines whether the synaptic weight potentiates or depresses.
engineering_relevance: This enables zero-bias, light-driven memory and processing for energy-efficient neuromorphic vision hardware with tunable bidirectional plasticity.
method: Measured photocurrent updates under 365 nm and 455 nm light pulses at zero bias
Used spectral light soaking, reverse-bias erasure tests, and optical simulations to identify defect-mediated mechanisms
Validated device-level learning in a digit-recognition network using measured weight updates
evidence_signal: At equal photon flux, 365 nm increased photocurrent by 38% while 455 nm decreased it, with up to 19 distinguishable levels per branch and 89% classification accuracy without noise (85% with measured noise).
watch_item: Performance depends on interface defect population and light spectrum, so fabrication variability and wavelength control may strongly affect reproducibility.
paper_title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
